defects.detail: source 'uirtūque bonum esse, ut dixit Pittacus' rendered 'a "virtuous good" as Pittacus said'; 'Nihil simile dissimili, & foli, & uni' rendered 'Nothing is like to the unlike, the solo, and the one'

reason: Follows the Latin closely throughout, including the Greek quotations via their Latin glosses; only awkward renderings of the Pittacus clause and the 'solo/one' phrase.

defects.detail: 'Luminis ornatum in quem dedit atque abatum' rendered 'into whom he gave and abated' (abatum = abbot/abbacy not recognised); 'in summulis' rendered 'in his summaries' rather than the Summulae

reason: Prose commentary and the verses with their interlinear glosses are all rendered; only the last verse line and 'summulis' are slightly off.
Dutch is rendered sentence by sentence, place names and margin notes included; nothing missing or added.
Argument, the Phaedrus verse quotations, and the Dio reference are all rendered faithfully; ends where the source breaks off.

defects.detail: meta asserts 'The word "proceeding" (pro-) from the bottom of page 11 is completed here as "ways"' -- the source carries only catchword των and no earlier page

reason: The Greek Timaeus paraphrase is rendered accurately (one portion, then double); the only problem is the meta claim about a 'pro-' fragment on page 11, which the source does not carry.

defects.detail: meta 'continues from page 138: because of this,' -- source is page 48 and begins ἔδοξέ τε ἡμῖν; no such text
τοῖν δυοῖν μεροῖν (the two portions) rendered 'two-thirds of the estate'
ἔθετο πρὸς Μικίωνα ... ἐθέλοντες ὁτιοῦν πάσχειν (we were willing to suffer anything) rendered as 'he made an agreement with Micion ... saying he was willing to suffer anything', subject shifted
Μικίωνι τὸ βαλανεῖον (make the bathhouse secure for Micion) rendered 'return the bathhouse to Micion'

reason: Narrative largely follows the Greek, but the two portions become 'two-thirds', the Micion agreement has its subject flipped, and a fabricated 'page 138' carry-over precedes it.

defects.detail: OCR of cursive kana such as 'およさわきをまくをあふらり' and 'ふいふよ梅かさね方には' rendered as confident lines ('The noise of the world is scattered', 'In the manner of the layering of plum blossoms') the source cannot support
'ふさき山には礼つきてなれ' rendered 'The mountain of the cape is marked by ritual'

reason: The source is near-unreadable handwriting OCR; the translation turns it into fluent poetic prose with no warning that the text is unclear.
Strabo on Crete rendered fully with all stadia figures, place names, the Homer, Aratus and Callimachus references, and the margin marker.

defects.detail: first line 'Fallere: et incultos aris aduertere crines' rendered 'me: and to turn my unkempt hair to the altars' -- the verb Fallere is dropped and a stray 'me:' added
'scelerumque ingentia femina mouit' rendered 'moved the huge woman of crimes' (ingentia is the object, not describing femina)

reason: Verse is rendered line by line and mostly accurate; the opening verb is lost and one clause has its syntax misread.
Long Latin argument on mineral waters and Paracelsus is rendered faithfully including margins and headings; notes only gloss terms actually present.

defects.detail: several OCR-damaged Hebrew stretches (e.g. 'ובלאר חורור פנימי של עשירי בבינוי בברכה', 'ואומר ... מחשב') are smoothed into readable English or elided with ellipses

reason: Follows the Toledot/tithe/Recanati argument closely including the Yod symbolism; some damaged passages are smoothed; Hebrew read at moderate confidence.
The quoted Ethiopic passage on Adam and the four elements, the author's aside, and the Wideburg reference are all rendered accurately; notes are interpretive.

defects.detail: meta 'continues from previous page: ury suffers due to the gap between his lifestyle and his limited means' -- no such text in the source, which begins في اجيالهم المتأخرة
'من العصايب والقبايل' (clans and tribes) rendered 'tribal groups and rebels'

reason: Ibn Khaldun's argument about stipends and the shrinking garrison is rendered accurately; a fabricated carry-over fragment and 'rebels' for tribes are the only slips.

defects.detail: '第一統三戸裕士軍' rendered 'First Section, Third Household, Yusa-ri village' -- a village name the source does not give
'巳酉式' (己酉 register, 1669) rendered 'Gisa, sixth year of the sexagenary cycle'
maternal grandfather's seat 晋山 rendered 'Jinyang'; 丙午式軍給者 rendered as 'Issued for the Byeong-o year military registration'

reason: Genealogy, ages, and margin son/grandson names are correct, but the register cycle year is misread and a village is supplied from garbled characters.
